clue.text: Eliot G's weaver protects international seamen

indicators.note: to protect is to wrap around, so the weaver's name surrounds the letter for international

parts.note: Silas Marner is George Eliot's weaver; the possessive 's is kept

explanation.surface: A novel's weaver is cast as a guardian of sailors from many nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliot G's' is George Eliot's, written surname first; her weaver is Silas MARNER, and the 's stays on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariners are sailors, so the word is a straight synonym for seamen.

clue.text: Claim to be confused regarding chemical processes in the body

definitions.text: regarding chemical processes in the body

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast gets muddled when it comes to biochemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' looks like part of the phrase 'to be confused', but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the set of chemical reactions in a living body; the adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: Farm labourer, lacking company, upset over a sports event

indicators.note: over means placed above, which in a down entry means before the A
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
lacking means without, so the letters for company are removed

parts.note: a cottager is a rural labourer living in a tied cottage

explanation.surface: A farmhand, sacked by his firm, is upset at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: COTTAGER loses CO to give TTAGER, which 'upset' turns into REGATT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat races, a sporting event on water.

clue.text: Family member found in Tyne and Wear region? That's a relief!

parts.note: Tyne and Wear lies in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
phew is an exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: A relative turns up in the north-east of England, to everyone's relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' suggests a hidden word, but it only links the definition to the pieces. Tyne and Wear is a county around Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a sibling's son, one kind of relative.

clue.text: Swimmer reveals what Ziggy Stardust had?

definitions.meaning: a fish of the goatfish family, eaten in the Mediterranean
David Bowie's character Ziggy Stardust wore a red hairstyle short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A fish reveals what Bowie's glam alter ego sported.
explanation.walkthrough: A mullet is also a haircut short at front and sides and long at the back; Ziggy's was dyed red.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish name doubles as a description of a red-dyed mullet haircut.

clue.text: Think of a number?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to reckon or suppose, as in 'I ... he'll come'

explanation.surface: A party trick: think of a number.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both reckoning something in your head and a written digit.

clue.text: Gather around extremely elegant bit of leg

indicators.note: around means the word for gathering goes round the picked letters

parts.note: to flock is to gather in a crowd

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of elegant

explanation.surface: People crowd round a shapely leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetlock is the joint above a horse's hoof, part of its leg.

clue.text: Relating to sexual intercourse, good for Catholic, single, to make attempt unaccompanied

indicators.note: good for Catholic means the letter for good takes the place of the letter for Catholic

parts.note: coital is the adjective from coitus, sexual intercourse
one means single

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about sex, religion and going solo.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is an idiom for acting by oneself without help.

clue.text: Go back on promise; EU manufacturing cut by 50% in recession

indicators.note: recession means going backwards, so the combined letters are reversed
cut by half means the back half of the word is removed

parts.note: generating means producing or manufacturing

explanation.surface: A news line about European industry halving in an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: GENERATING halved is GENER; EU + GENER reversed gives the answer. 'recession' suggests economics but means reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue (more usually renege) is to break a promise or commitment.

clue.text: Drag spare tyre over

indicators.note: over signals that the word for the belly roll is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a spare tyre is slang for a roll of belly fat, a gut

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a spare wheel across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare tyre' is British slang for a roll of fat round the waist, not a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To tug is to pull hard, a synonym of drag.

clue.text: A boring president, awfully mundane

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters of the combination are reordered

explanation.surface: A dull head of state, terribly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' puts A inside PRESIDENT; 'awfully' then rearranges all ten letters. 'boring' looks like a second definition but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and commonplace, the same as mundane.

clue.text: Flower without bit of colour is flatter

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the flower's name

parts.note: a buttercup is a yellow wild flower

indicators.note: a bit of the word colour is its first letter

explanation.surface: A flower missing a touch of colour looks flatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like a comparative adjective describing the flower, but it is the verb, to praise insincerely.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter up is an idiom for flattering someone to win favour.

clue.text: Love selection of fruit

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a range is a selection of goods on offer

explanation.surface: Someone adores a mixed assortment of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus fruit, an example of the general class.

clue.text: Storyteller is weird? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word is dropped, here the front four letters

parts.note: peculiar means strange or weird

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a teller of tales is odd, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it tells you to lose half of PECULIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller is one who tells stories, a euphemism for someone who tells untruths.

clue.text: Lousy trio performing in a wanton manner

indicators.note: performing suggests acting out, so the letters are rearranged into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A poor three-piece band plays with wild abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotously means in a wild, unrestrained way, which is what wantonly describes.

clue.text: Perhaps Elizabeth caught person with key bounding to work

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: bounding means forming the boundary of, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: a locker is someone who locks up, so holds a key
W is the physics symbol for work

explanation.surface: A keyholder is caught leaping off to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounding' suggests leaping but means enclosing. W for work comes from physics. Elizabeth Tower is the official name of the London clock tower housing Big Ben.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Tower at Westminster is an example of a tower bearing a clock, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Charlie and Miss Germany have come to a standstill

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to miss is to lose, as with a chance
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Charlie and Miss Germany have halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Germany' looks like a beauty queen, but splits into LOSE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To close down is to cease operating, i.e. halt.

clue.text: Dog left for son is very memorable

indicators.note: left for son means the letter for left takes the place of the letter for son

parts.note: the red setter is the Irish setter breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog bequeathed to someone's boy is unforgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'bequeathed' but is L, replacing the S of REDSETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a notable one, marked in red on old calendars.

clue.text: Commanding officer helping guards working in ceremony

indicators.note: to guard is to hold inside, so the word for helping encloses the word for working

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: An officer in command assists the guards working at a state ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronation is the formal ceremony of crowning a monarch.

clue.text: Be responsible for amputee's revolutionary climbing trousers

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going up, so the letters read backwards
to trouser is to pocket, so the two words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A one-legged revolutionary's trousers for climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is the verb, to pocket: the letters EESREVO sit inside 'amputee's revolutionary', and 'climbing' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, being in charge of something.

clue.text: Warn Conservative to drop sell-off

indicators.note: in a down clue drop means move lower, so the letter for Conservative slides further down the word

parts.note: to caution is to warn

explanation.surface: Telling a Tory to abandon a privatisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale to the highest bidder, a kind of selling off.

clue.text: A date for one goes ahead? Blimey!

indicators.note: goes ahead says the piece for 'for one' is placed in front of the date

parts.note: e.g., for example, means 'for one'
AD, anno domini, is used in dates

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a lone diner's booking still stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes ahead' looks like 'is not cancelled', but it is a placing instruction; 'A date' is not a romantic outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, just as Blimey is.

clue.text: Terrible serve results in scowl, perhaps

parts.note: grim means dreadful or terrible
an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player's awful serve brings a scowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible serve' reads as a bad shot, but an ace is a winning serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression; a scowl is one example.

clue.text: Baby lettuce plant

parts.note: cos is a variety of lettuce, romaine
to set is to plant, as seeds or seedlings

explanation.surface: A young lettuce plant in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' reads as an adjective, as in baby lettuce, but it is the verb meaning to pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to pamper them, which is what cosset means.

clue.text: Announced "Oh, I see, chasing that woman is daring"

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the sounded letters come after the pronoun

parts.note: her refers to that woman

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the phrase is replaced by letters that sound like it

parts.note: the phrase spoken sounds like the three letters O, I, C

explanation.surface: Someone declares, with sudden understanding, that pursuing a particular woman takes nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic means bold and courageous, a synonym of daring.

clue.text: Learn viral video contains PM scratching head

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the internet clip goes round the trimmed name

parts.note: a meme is an image or video widely shared online

indicators.note: scratching means deleting, and head is the first letter, so the name loses its opening

parts.note: Boris Johnson was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A viral clip of the Prime Minister puzzled, scratching his head, to be learnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' suggests puzzlement but tells you to drop the B from BORIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To memorise is to commit to memory, which is to learn by heart.

clue.text: Promising Stokes will replace Anderson at first is questionable

indicators.note: will replace means one letter takes the place of another in the word for promising
at first means only the initial letters of the two cricketers' names take part in the swap

parts.note: auspicious means showing promise of success
James Anderson, the England fast bowler, reduced to his initial
Ben Stokes, the England all-rounder, reduced to his initial

explanation.surface: A cricket selection note: Stokes will take Anderson's place in the opening line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Stokes and James Anderson are England cricketers; their initials S and A are swapped at the front of AUSPICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicious can mean arousing doubt, so it matches questionable.

clue.text: Overweight female goes right to the back

indicators.note: goes right means the letter shifts towards the right within the word

parts.note: fat means overweight

explanation.surface: An overweight woman heads straight to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is a nautical word for towards the stern, the back of a vessel.

clue.text: Trust those following Orwell regularly

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for those goes behind the picked letters
regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, the even ones of Orwell

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word meaning that or those

explanation.surface: Faith in the disciples of George Orwell, as a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to depend on or have faith in them.

clue.text: I twerk with an eccentric in warm clothing?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dances provocatively alongside an oddball, while wrapped up warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear means knitted garments such as jumpers, typically worn for warmth; the question mark marks the loose fit.
